A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DataDecide study and contain readable main text, Appendices A–C, six figures, and four tables. The extensive layout changes do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled pretraining experiments across 25 data recipes and 14 model scales, with prediction and evaluation results in Figures 1–6 and Table 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original pretraining experiments and their empirical results, including the appendix comparison of scaling-law prediction errors.

M1.justification: The model architectures, single-scale ranking procedure, and scaling-law fitting procedures in Section 2.2 and Appendix C are retained. Table 3's normalization revision concerns the reported evaluation metrics; no separate algorithm or model-component change is described.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 25 pretraining recipes, ten OLMES benchmarks, and supplementary Minerva, GSM8K, MBPP, and HumanEval evaluations. The new Common Crawl citation identifies an already-used source.

E2.justification: Figure 3 and Table 4 retain the same comparison between single-scale ranking and eight scaling-law variants, including helper-point, checkpoint-filtering, and single-step variants.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes token- and character-length normalization from P(c|context)/length to log(P(c|context))/length. This revises the stated metric calculation, while model configurations, budgets, benchmark sampling, and testing procedures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: The proxy-metric comparisons, noise-versus-spread analysis, code/math case study, and scaling-law variant analyses are retained in Sections 3.2–3.4 and Appendix C. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed means and standard deviations for single-scale predictions and the same single fully trained seed for scaling-law comparisons. No uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 retain the same plotted results, and every prediction-error entry in Table 4 is unchanged; the default three-parameter variant remains at 6.5 relative error and 3.1 absolute error. No revised outcomes accompany the normalization-definition edit.

T1.justification: Table 3 inserts a logarithm into both length-normalization definitions, a mathematically non-equivalent revision. The decision-accuracy definition and scaling-law equations remain unchanged, with no added assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims: the DataDecide suite, strong single-scale prediction, no frontier improvement from eight scaling-law baselines, and improved predictability using continuous proxy metrics.

C2.justification: The explanations involving crossovers, run-to-run noise, and performance spread are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning the token-to-parameter ratio, model scales, data recipes, and evaluation coverage.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Common Crawl homepage reference with an access date, providing an additional pointer to an existing data source. Table 2's hyperparameters, the hardware-cost disclosure, and the DataDecide collection link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds an explicit Common Crawl reference linked from Table 1. Existing cited works and the substantive research-positioning discussion are retained; other bibliography edits concern formatting and publication metadata.

P1.justification: The scientific prose and section sequence are essentially unchanged. Limited editorial changes include renaming 'Ethics Statement' to 'Impact Statement', adding correspondence and conference information, and changing bibliography style.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column format to a two-column conference layout, with redesigned headers and title placement. Existing figures are resized and relocated, Figures 2–3 and 4–5 are grouped on shared pages, and appendix Tables 2–4 are consolidated onto one page.

improvement.justification: Replacing probability/length with log-probability/length in Table 3 improves the stated length-normalization specification, while the Common Crawl reference improves source attribution and access information. These are limited documentation gains: the empirical evidence and conclusions are unchanged, and the extensive reformatting does not establish a larger quality improvement.
